title: I built an animation builder entirely with AI: an AI agent turns gameplay video into rigged game animations
author: Organic-Shame-4520
selftext:
I've been building an animation builder entirely with AI: all the code, and the work inside the tool too. An AI agent drives it, and it turns a video into game animations.

This demo is a non-human boss, the Scorpionlord from Black Myth: Wukong, taken from a YouTube boss guide (credit: Wilstorm Gaming, [How to beat The Scorpionlord](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bKme0WclwkY)).

What the AI did, start to finish:

* **Extracted the segments:** downloaded the video, found each attack, and cut motion-only clips (skipping the guide's pause frames).
* **Built the rig:** worked out the creature's body plan and made a 40-joint skeleton to match: pincer arms, digitigrade legs, a 12-segment tail with a stinger.
* **Animated 10 moves:** idle, stalk, tail stab, spin sweep, pincer combo, somersault tail plunge, aerial spin slash, aerial tail cyclone, burrow ambush, four-part combo.
* **Checked its own work:** every clip stays within the joint limits it set for each bone, with no frame-to-frame pops, and the file passes the standard glTF validator.
* **Built this review page:** each animation plays next to the clip it came from.

Human characters are captured from video with pose tracking. A scorpion can't be tracked that way, so here the AI keyed the motion from the footage instead. The mesh is placeholder blocks; the motion is the point.

Feedback welcome, especially on the aerial moves.
